defects.statement: Fleet-health telemetry never observed Bahia-published observables. Publisher.PublishSignedEventWithResults records each signed event in nostr_events before the first relay attempt, and Subscriber.handleEvent skips every handler when Record reports inserted=false, so the relay echo of a self-published event never reached telemetryProvider.ObserveNostrEvent. This affected the existing runtime managed-instance projection as well as the new route projection.
defects.fix: Subscriber gained WithObserver for idempotent read-side projections that run for every validated, durably persisted event regardless of insert state; fleet-health telemetry is registered as an observer while side-effect handlers remain gated.

defects.statement: The fleet-health domain vocabulary was duplicated: boundedFleetDomain and renderNostrFleetHealthMetrics each held their own list, so a domain could be classified without being exported.
defects.fix: Single nostrFleetHealthDomains list read by both classification and rendering.

defects.statement: RouteCanaryGate.record persists gate outcomes, including an immediately opened outage, through RouteCanaryRepository.UpsertStateWithEvent only; the gate holds no events.Publisher, so gate outcomes never reach the projector directly. A gate-declared outage reaches Nostr only when the supervisor later reports a transition for that route, and not at all while it persists with an unchanged classification, because the supervisor sees the already-open state and reports no transition. Consequence found by independent review of the combined tree (integration 22b84636): after a supervisor-opened outage, a passing post-deploy gate saved Recovered with thresholds 1/1 and published nothing, later sweeps saw a closed route_ok and reported no transition, so 30315/30900 and bahia_fleet_health_nostr_entities{domain="route",status="unhealthy"} stayed on the outage indefinitely and route.canary_recovered was never announced.
defects.fix: RouteCanaryGate now takes an events.Publisher (wired to the shared in-process bus in internal/app/app.go) and, after UpsertStateWithEvent succeeds, publishes through publishRouteCanaryTransition, the single transition-publishing implementation the supervisor also uses (routeCanaryTransitionEvent builds the event). Gate and supervisor therefore announce identical RouteCanaryChanged payloads, event types and severities. Publication happens only for persisted transitions, on context.WithoutCancel so a canceled deployment still announces a durable transition; rollback remains on its own non-canceled context. Owner note superseded: the gate change was made in the integration fix branch (task/bahia-canary-integration-fix-go).

defects.statement: Fleet-health telemetry keeps its projection in memory and the subscriber backfills from the latest persisted created_at, so after a restart subject gauges (all domains, including route) start empty until new observables arrive; a long-running outage is uncounted until its next transition.
defects.owner_note: Pre-existing fleet-health ingestion design; needs a follow-up bead for replaceable-state hydration.

defects.statement: Route state is projected on transition only, so a route whose outage opened before the projector was deployed is projected on its next transition.
defects.owner_note: Resolved together with D4 by a startup projection of current durable route state, or by hydration; needs a follow-up bead.

defects.statement: After fleet-health telemetry moved to WithObserver it observes every delivery of an event (relay echo, reconnect overlap, one copy per relay). bahia_fleet_health_projector_errors_total was incremented per delivery on both rejection paths (unattributable observable, entity limit reached), so one bad event redelivered N times counted N errors.
defects.fix: Projection errors are counted once per event ID through a bounded FIFO set sized to the entity limit (content-derived ID when an event carries none). Entity state, last event and last ingested timestamps were already redelivery-idempotent because they move only for a strictly newer created_at; heartbeat lag derives from the event's created_at; the relay CLOSED counter is not on the event path.
